status: implemented opt-in; not registered or strength-tested
scope: Classic Normal only; default absent behavior byte-identical

primary_research.title: A formal analysis and taxonomy of task allocation in multi-robot systems
primary_research.authors: Brian P. Gerkey and Maja J. Mataric
primary_research.use: Motivates explicit robot-task utility and capability allocation. This mechanism is a narrow Stratego hypothesis, not a performance claim from the paper.

problem: Independent persistent goals can send several capable attackers toward one disclosed weak enemy while an uncovered disclosed stronger enemy can only be defeated by the redundant stronger pursuer.
difference_from_previous_work: Coordinates distinct existing combat tasks using unchanged native utilities. Does not add information rewards, rank guesses, activation pressure, loop penalties, search depth, sampling, specialist material bonuses or score coefficients.
public_inputs: Own ranks and public legal moves including two-squares history
Enemy occupancy and CELL_REVEALED ranks only
Existing native hidden expected gains from public remaining-rank counts and movement
algorithm: Calculate each actor original goal and exact unchanged native target utilities using original reachability: friendly blockers; enemy cells endpoints, never transit.
For every originally served disclosed mobile target, lock the highest original utility primary pursuer; stable source-square scan order breaks ties. Preserve all unmatched and nonpositive goals.

Consider only positive-utility redundant pursuers; exclude Miner and Spy specialists. Alternative must be uncovered by every original active goal, disclosed mobile, reachable, positive native utility, and a strict winning capture for this actor. Equal trades and losing new assignments are excluded.
Reassign at most one actor, choosing the largest positive alternative native task utility, stable source/target square order. Every other original goal is preserved.
Use ordinary persistent goal transfer and unchanged candidate scoring. Captures, immediate wins, threat computation, one-ply Flag defense, randomness and legal move generation are unchanged.

fixture.enemy_hidden: 38 enemy home slots excluding30 and35; all hidden low nibbles ignored
fixture.interpretation: Costs one point of redundant pursuit utility to add a25-point distinct useful objective. This does not maximize summed actor utility.

retrospective_evidence: task-assignment-opportunities.json reproduces1459 native goals across140 roots. Six roots have known-mobile duplication with a reachable uncovered alternative before stricter v1 capability/positive/primary/specialist filters. That is an opportunity upper bound, not six demonstrated improvements.
limits: Duplicate pursuit can create valuable capture nets or second-wave support; reallocating it can weaken tactics.
Enemy tasks move and native square goals can become obsolete.
An existing utility-positive target can still be strategically poor; no global win or safety guarantee.
One reassignment per decision is a deliberately narrow hypothesis, not full multi-unit scheduling.
No saved match or validation seed was used to tune the mechanism.
cost: One original source BFS and one final goal BFS per active actor as baseline, plus at most40x40 cached utilities and bounded scans; per-decision scratch is desktop opt-in only.
strict_retrospective_evidence: Stricter v1 filtering finds3 concrete roots in1 of14 games (140 sampled roots), with actor-utility costs17,7,1 and distinct-task gains18,31,37. Sparse mechanism; no claim of frequent failures or improved strength.
